sections.title: Sections
sections.lede: The catalogue is a frozen public contract – a number is never reused, and a retired section becomes a no-op that says so.
sections.reportOnlyTitle: Report only - there is nothing to select
sections.detailReportOnly: This section writes a report and deletes nothing.
sections.detailNothing: Nothing declared on this machine right now.
sections.emptyBody: All {{count}} are still there. The filter is narrow.
sections.policySummary: What the four run policies mean
sections.policyBody: <1>Safe</1> runs on its own. <3>Opt-in</3> only runs if you name it. <5>Deep</5> needs an extra confirmation on top. <7>Interactive</7> needs you to pick the items, one by one.
sections.selBlocked: Sections {{ids}} need you to choose items first. Nothing was run.
picker.section.17.title: Stale build artefacts
picker.section.17.lede: node_modules, target, .gradle and friends, in projects nothing has touched for months. Rebuilt by the project’s own install or build command.
picker.section.18.title: Partial downloads
picker.section.18.lede: Half-finished downloads left behind by browsers and download managers. Only Downloads – never Desktop, never Documents.
picker.section.19.title: Large or old files
picker.section.19.lede: Downloads first. You can add folders, inspect each result, and choose what goes to the Recycle Bin.
picker.section.23.title: Orphaned application data
picker.section.23.lede: AppData folders belonging to programs that are no longer installed. Fails closed: if the registry cannot be read, nothing is offered.
picker.section.26.title: Uninstall programs and Store apps you pick
picker.section.26.lede: Desktop programs run their own uninstallers, one at a time; Store apps are removed for this Windows account. Both are permanent, and a second list then offers what they left behind.
picker.section.27.title: Leftovers of uninstalled programs
picker.section.27.lede: What uninstalled programs left where nothing installed, registered or running still uses it. Needs administrator permission. Folders and shortcuts go to the Recycle Bin; everything else is backed up first.
picker.section.30.title: Windows updates you pick
picker.section.30.lede: Security, quality and Defender updates and the malicious software removal tool, as Windows Update lists them for this PC. Windows Update fetches each one; windowsweep never restarts your PC.
picker.section.31.title: Driver updates and old driver packages
picker.section.31.lede: Driver updates from Windows Update, and old packages left in the driver store. The newest two of each driver always stay, so Device Manager’s Roll Back keeps working. BIOS and firmware updates are never offered, and your PC maker’s own driver tool is named, never run.
picker.section.32.title: App updates you pick
picker.section.32.lede: winget fetches each update from its publisher, one at a time. An app that is running is skipped, and an installer that changes the whole PC may show its own Windows permission prompt.
picker.ranNote: <1>Ran</1> counts the days since Windows last saw each program start. Windows tells only an elevated window, so this list shows a dash.
picker.fate27.registry: Backed up to a .reg file first; double-clicking that file puts the key back
picker.fate27.startup: Starts {{target}}, which is gone · backed up to a .reg file first
picker.fate27.task: Exported to an XML file first; Task Scheduler can import it back
picker.runningHint: Close it first, or it is skipped
picker.report.note: Both lists are for reading. Section 31 changes nothing in them; Device Manager shows the same devices and drivers.
picker.dataIntro: Downloads is scanned by default. Add another folder only when you choose it.
picker.dataThresholds: Large: {{large}} MB or more. Old: {{days}} days or more by the timestamp shown on each row. Change the limits in Settings.
picker.dataUnmeasured: No files measured for this folder scope yet.
picker.dataNotAskedTitle: This folder scope has not been scanned.
picker.dataNotAskedBody: Use Scan these folders above to measure files. Nothing is selected or removed by a scan.
picker.dataOldCaution: “Old” means the recorded timestamp passed the idle window. It does not prove the file is unneeded. Nothing is selected until you choose a row.
picker.notAskedBody: A dry-run costs nothing and deletes nothing.
picker.adminScanBody: A dry-run of these leftovers asks Windows for administrator permission. Declining scans nothing, and nothing is removed.
picker.notAskedInstallBody: A dry-run lists what is available. Nothing is installed until you choose rows and confirm.
picker.devOff: Developer mode is off, so the engine skips this one. Turn it on in Settings first.
picker.searchEmptyBody: Clear the filter and the candidates come back.
picker.note: <1>Nothing here is pre-selected, on purpose.</1> These nine sections refuse to act on <3>--yes</3> alone. A scripted selection (<5>--select</5> or <7>--select-file</7>) counts as a person choosing; a refused row cannot be selected.
picker.fileSummary: Drive this from a file instead
picker.fileBody: A plain UTF-8 file with one full path per line is matched, case-insensitively, against the candidates this section offers. A line that matches nothing is warned about individually rather than failing the run.
picker.fileTipPurpose: <1>Purpose: </1>One full path per line; each is matched against the candidates a section offers.
picker.fileIdle: Drop a selection file here, or choose one
picker.fileHint: .txt or .list · up to 256 KB · one full path per line
picker.fileTooBig: That file is {{size}} - the limit is 256 KB
picker.fileUnreadable: That file could not be read.
picker.download.knownPlusUnknown_one: {{size}} to download, plus {{count}} of unknown size
picker.download.knownPlusUnknown_other: {{size}} to download, plus {{count}} of unknown size
picker.installLine.wu: Windows updates come from Windows Update, one at a time.
picker.installLine.drivers: Drivers come from Windows Update, one at a time.
picker.installLine.old: Old driver packages leave the driver store; the newest two of each driver stay.
picker.installLine.winget: App updates come from each publisher through winget, one at a time; a running app is skipped.
picker.installLine.elevated: Windows asks for your permission first.
picker.installLine.restart: windowsweep never restarts your PC; Windows says when a restart is due.
picker.kept_one: {{count}} more row stays chosen in section {{list}}; it runs separately.
picker.kept_other: {{count}} more rows stay chosen in section {{list}}; they run separately.
picker.keptAcross_other: {{count}} more rows stay chosen in sections {{list}}; they run separately.
picker.nothingHereBody: This section found no candidates on this machine. That is the good outcome, not an error.
picker.consequence: The Recycle Bin can be emptied later. Permanent has no undo.
picker.consequence17: Section 17's rows are deleted outright whichever you choose.
picker.consequence19: Personal files selected in section 19 go to the Recycle Bin in this window.
picker.consequence26: Uninstalling is permanent whichever mode you choose, and a broken entry is cleared from Apps after a .reg backup. A second list then offers what the removed programs left.
picker.consequence27: Section 27 needs administrator permission. Registry keys and startup entries are backed up to .reg files in the run's registry-backups folder first, and a key whose backup cannot be written is kept.
picker.confirmBody: They do not go to the Recycle Bin. Permanent has no undo.
picker.confirmUninstallTitle: Uninstall the chosen programs and apps?
picker.confirmUninstall.desktop: Each desktop program runs its own uninstaller, one at a time. One without a silent form opens its own window; finish it there.
picker.confirmUninstall.store: Store apps are removed for this Windows account only.
picker.confirmUninstall.broken: A broken entry’s uninstaller is gone, so the entry is cleared from Apps after a .reg backup.
picker.confirmUninstall.after: None of this goes to the Recycle Bin. A second list then offers what the programs left.
picker.confirmUninstall.others: The other rows you chose follow the choice in the bar.
picker.installConfirm.title: {{verb}}?
picker.installConfirm.wu: Windows Update downloads each update, one at a time.
picker.installConfirm.firmware: BIOS and firmware updates are never offered.
picker.installConfirm.makerTool: Your PC maker’s own driver tool is named in the log, never run.
picker.installConfirm.winget: winget fetches each app update from its publisher, one at a time. An app that is running is skipped, and an installer that changes the whole PC may show its own Windows permission prompt.
picker.installConfirm.old: Old driver packages are deleted from the driver store, not moved to the Recycle Bin. The newest two of each driver always stay, so Device Manager’s Roll Back keeps working.
picker.installConfirm.admin: Windows updates and drivers need an elevated window, so Windows asks for your permission first.
picker.installConfirm.restart: windowsweep never restarts your PC. When an update needs a restart, Windows says so.
elevation.title_one: {{count}} section needs Windows to ask your permission.
elevation.title_other: {{count}} sections need Windows to ask your permission.
elevation.lede: windowsweep <1>never elevates itself</1>. When you ask for one of these, it opens a second, elevated window that does that work and writes its own report. This window keeps running, unelevated, and shows you the log as it arrives.
elevation.whatHappens: What happens when you press it
elevation.step.asks.title: Windows asks you.
elevation.step.asks.body: The standard User Account Control prompt, from Windows, not from windowsweep. If you say no, nothing happens and nothing is written.
elevation.step.second.title: A second window opens.
elevation.step.second.body: It runs only the sections you chose, with <1>--reports-dir</1> and <3>--logs-dir</3> pointed at this run’s folder.
elevation.step.tails.title: This window tails the log.
elevation.step.tails.body: You watch it from here. The elevated window closes itself when it is done, and its exit code comes back to this one.
elevation.step.reports.title: Both reports land side by side.
elevation.hiberfilLegend: What to do with the hibernation file
elevation.devOff: Developer mode is off, so the engine skips this one. Turn it on in Settings first.
elevation.deepGateTitle: These sections make lasting changes. Read the ones you chose before continuing.
elevation.deepGateBody: windowsweep will not run them unattended until you say you know that – it passes <3>--i-understand-deep</3>, and nothing else in this window does.
elevation.deepWhat.15: <1>Hibernation file.</1> Turning it off removes <3>hiberfil.sys</3> and with it Hibernate, Fast Startup and hibernate-on-critical-battery. Sleep still works. Reduced keeps Fast Startup at a smaller file.
elevation.deepWhat.16: <1>Event logs.</1> Clearing them is permanent and removes the history a technician would use to diagnose a problem.
elevation.deepWhat.20: <1>WSL disk images.</1> Compaction stops Docker Desktop and every WSL distro first. Start Docker again afterwards.
elevation.deepWhat.29: <1>Chrome on-device AI model.</1> This sets a Windows policy that removes the model and prevents it returning. Chrome will say ‘Managed by your organization’ for that policy.
elevation.deepConfirm: I understand what these do. Run the ones I chose.
elevation.deepConfirmAria: I understand what these sections do
elevation.blockedNone: Choose at least one section first.
elevation.blockedDeep: Confirm you understand the deep sections above.
elevation.childReport: The elevated window reclaimed {{amount}} across $t(elevation.countSteps, {"count": {{ran}} }), and skipped {{skipped}}.
elevation.measureNote: A scan can measure these sections without administrator rights. It cannot clear them.
elevation.measured: Measured {{amount}} across the sections you chose. Nothing was deleted, and no permission was needed to look.
elevation.picked.title: Installing Windows updates and drivers needs permission too
elevation.picked.lede: Sections 30 and 31 list what is available without asking. You pick rows on the Choose screen, and installing them runs in an elevated window, the way the steps above describe.
elevation.picked.30: Listing needs no permission. Installing the updates you pick does.
elevation.picked.31: Driver updates list without permission; old driver packages list only in an elevated window. Installing a driver or removing a package needs permission.
elevation.picked.note32: App updates in section 32 run without one. An installer that changes the whole PC shows its own Windows permission prompt.
elevation.smartScreenSummary: Windows may warn you the first time you install this
elevation.smartScreenWhy: The installer is not signed with a paid code-signing certificate, so Microsoft SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC” on first run. That is a statement about the certificate, not about the file.
elevation.smartScreenHow: Choose More info and then Run anyway. You can verify what you downloaded first: every release publishes a SHA-256 checksum for each installer, and a minisign signature the app’s own updater checks. Neither is a code-signing certificate – they prove the file is the one that was built, not who built it. The source is public.
elevation.smartScreenWhyHere: This note is here rather than hidden because meeting that dialog unexplained is worse than reading about it in advance.
